Earnings Call Transcript
Paycom (PAYC) Q3 2025 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

Nov 6, 2025 at 10:20AM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


Date
Wednesday, November 5, 2025 at 5 p.m. ET
Call participants
Chief Executive Officer — Chad Richison
Chief Financial Officer — Robert Foster
Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email
[email protected]
Takeaways
Total Revenues (Q3 2025)
-- $493 million, representing 9.1% year-over-year growth.
Recurring and Other Revenues (Q3 2025)
-- $467 million, up 10.6% year-over-year.
Interest on Funds Held for Clients (Q3 2025)
-- $27 million, a decrease of 11% year-over-year.
GAAP Net Income (Q3 2025)
-- $111 million, or $1.96 per diluted share, including a one-time, tax-adjusted gain of $26 million ($0.47 per diluted share) from a naming rights agreement modification.
Non-GAAP net income for the third quarter
-- $110 million, representing a 17% year-over-year increase; $1.94 per diluted share.
Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter
-- $194 million, growing 13% year-over-year; adjusted EBITDA margin reached 39%, an increase of 150 basis points.
AI-Focused CapEx
-- Approximately $100 million invested in Phoenix and Oklahoma City data centers to support iOne; this spend is now largely complete.
Share Repurchases
-- $319 million in common stock repurchased in the open market during the quarter, reducing shares outstanding by almost 3% as of August 2025.
Dividends Paid Since 2023
-- Approximately $213 million returned to shareholders.
Remaining Buyback Authorization
-- Approximately $1.1 billion available as of October 31, 2025, with an undrawn $1 billion revolving credit facility.
Cash and Debt Position
-- Cash and cash equivalents stand at $375 million; no outstanding debt.
Average Daily Client Funds
-- Averaged $2.5 billion, up 9% year-over-year.
Full-Year Revenue Guidance
-- Projected range of $2.045 billion to $2.055 billion, midpoint growth of 9% year-over-year.
Full-Year Recurring and Other Revenue Guidance
-- Expected organic growth of 10% year-over-year.
Interest on Client Funds Guidance
-- Full-year interest anticipated at $113 million, a 10% year-over-year decline, assuming one more rate cut in 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA Guidance
-- Range of $872 million to $882 million for the year, implying a 160 basis point margin expansion to approximately 43% at midpoint.
Stock Compensation Expense
-- Forecasted at approximately 7% of revenues for the year.
Third-Quarter Dividend
-- Board approved a quarterly dividend of $0.0375 per share, payable in mid-December.
Product Launch: iOne
-- iOne, the command-driven AI product, was launched to 100% of the client base and is driving increased engagement, especially among C-suite and newly onboarded client employees.
Product Launch: Betty
-- Betty payroll automation reduces payroll process labor by up to 90% and cuts time spent on payroll error corrections by up to 85%, with recent client wins attributed to its adoption.
Client Satisfaction Metrics
-- Reported year-over-year decline in internal support tickets and client call volume by 20%-30%.
Workforce Reduction
-- Approximately 500 administrative employees let go as development backlog was released; effects expected in 2026, not fully reflected in current quarter results.
Summary
The call highlighted that
Paycom Software

(
PAYC

0.74%
)
completed a front-loaded $100 million investment in AI-centric data center infrastructure, positioning itself to support growing AI product adoption and automation initiatives. Management reiterated that current momentum places the company on track to surpass its full-year financial goals, with organic revenue gains and near-record adjusted EBITDA margins. The newly launched iOne platform has already achieved widespread adoption and is significantly changing usage patterns, particularly among executive users who previously did not routinely interface with HCM software.
Robert Foster stated, "we launched our most advanced automation solution ever, iOne, which is now enabled to our entire client base," confirming universal rollout and emphasizing product differentiation.
Chad Richison confirmed that "the more of our product that you have that you're utilizing, the more access to the information that you have," directly tying product attach rates to incremental user value and streamlined adoption.
Management expects AI infrastructure spending levels seen in Q3 to be nonrecurring, indicating materially lower CapEx for similar initiatives in future periods.
Leadership reported that automation advances have enabled measurable operational efficiencies, evidenced by GAAP and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion and declining support volumes.
No material changes were noted in employment levels within client companies apart from natural stability outside of COVID-affected periods.
Operational cost improvements were attributed to both automation and a one-time reduction in administrative headcount, which is anticipated to deliver greater cost benefits in future periods.
Industry glossary
HCM (Human Capital Management)
: Integrated software suite for managing workforce processes including payroll, talent acquisition, and time tracking.
Betty
: Proprietary Paycom Software payroll automation system designed to minimize manual intervention and errors.
iOne
: Paycom Software's command-driven AI platform intended to automate HR data access and process navigation.
LLM (Large Language Model)
: Advanced AI model capable of processing and generating human-like language based on extensive data sets.

Chad Richison:
Thanks, James, and thank you to everyone joining our call today. I'll briefly comment on third-quarter results and recent product innovations. I'll then turn it over to Bob for a review of our third-quarter results and our full-year guidance. We will then take questions. Let's get started. Third-quarter results came in strong with double-digit organic recurring revenue growth and continued margin expansion, setting us up to exceed our full-year financial plan for 2025. In addition to strong financials, we also executed the launch of our award-winning and industry-first command-driven AI product iOne.
Now enabled across our entire client base, iOne is transforming how our clients and their employees engage with their HR and payroll data. iOne has already successfully responded to millions of queries from employees, managers, and executives, extending the power of full solution automation. We are seeing a dramatic uptick in usage, especially among new users, which include the C-suite and newly onboarded employees of our clients. The intuitive nature of iOne means new employees no longer need training on the system and are able to utilize the full solution upon hire. I'm particularly encouraged by the engagement we are seeing among the C-suite. Traditionally, executives have not been daily users of HCM.
With iOne, thousands of C-suite executives are already pulling data and insights directly from the Paycom Software, Inc. system, and the feedback has been phenomenal. I'm confident that command-driven functionality is the future for all software. Betty is another example of automation that delivers significant ROI and is driving new sales. This award-winning payroll solution reduces payroll process labor by up to 90% while also cutting the time spent correcting payroll errors by up to 85%. Betty not only protects employees against insufficient funds by ensuring the payroll is correct prior to payday, but it also eliminates human interaction with non-revenue-generating tasks associated with voided payments, check reversals, ledger updates, post-payroll adjustments, just to name a few.
Betty also enhances payroll compliance, ensuring accurate tax withholding, along with wage and hour accuracy, which reduces employer liability because employees have control over the accuracy of their check. Additionally, automation and perfect payroll with Betty is also attracting former clients back to Paycom Software, Inc. Recently, two clients who were not previous Betty users came back to Paycom Software, Inc. thanks to Betty. One of these was a large auto group who, after leaving Paycom Software, Inc., had numerous issues processing multiple payrolls across their more than 25 locations that impacted their employees. They quickly realized the mistake they made and reached out to us to come back.
Upon their return, they were quick to adopt Betty because of the payroll automation and paycheck transparency. The second example of an organization returning was a manufacturing company whose employees quickly voiced frustration over the switch away from Paycom Software, Inc., especially managers who lost access to the information they were accustomed to, resulting in a slowdown in revenue-generating work. This organization pointed to Betty as a significant reason for the return and a game-changer with 100% accurate payrolls, thanks to Betty identifying and notifying employees of items that need attention prior to payday.
Betty continues to be a powerful differentiator for us in the market as we continue to drive even more automation and deliver very strong ROI to our clients. To facilitate the automation experience, including iOne and future AI developments in the pipeline, we significantly expanded our data center capabilities, spending roughly $100 million of AI-focused CapEx on our Phoenix and Oklahoma City data centers. We front-loaded this CapEx to match the timing of our iOne rollout in Q3.
Owning and operating advanced data centers is a sustainable competitive advantage for Paycom Software, Inc., particularly for clients who have reservations about opening up their critical data to external LLMs. iOne, hosted by Paycom Software, Inc., only draws from Paycom Software, Inc.'s single database, which eliminates conflicts created by inconsistent or duplicative external datasets, significantly improving data integrity and the quality of the user experience. Thanks to our product innovation and our focus on world-class service, client satisfaction trends remain strong. We provide high-touch personal service, and our clients appreciate our service levels now more than ever. We complement our high-touch service model with full solution automation, which drives service operation efficiency.
As a result, we've seen a 20% to 30% year-over-year decline in internal tickets and inbound client call volume. These are positive influencers on client satisfaction. With our strong third-quarter results and the outlook for the remainder of 2025, we are set to deliver a milestone year with over $2 billion in total revenues, all through organic growth and near-record level adjusted EBITDA margins. Paycom Software, Inc. has been leading our industry in innovation and client ROI achievements since we were founded. Now, with automated products like iOne, Betty, and Gone, we are well-positioned for continued strong performance in the future.
I want to thank all of our employees for their consistent contribution to Paycom Software, Inc.'s success and also thank our clients for trusting us to deliver unmatched value through full solution automation. With that, let me turn it over to Bob.

Our single database in our owned and operated data centers are competitive differentiators that enable us to rapidly develop and deploy new automations to benefit all our clients. During the quarter, we launched our most advanced automation solution ever, iOne, which is now enabled to our entire client base. To support iOne, we've front-loaded a significant CapEx investment in advanced AI hardware and equipment within our data centers. More specifically, we invested approximately $100 million into our data centers, and that spend is now largely complete. This investment provides us a multi-year capacity runway to support our AI initiatives.
Over the last two months, we repurchased $319 million of common stock in the open market, buying back over 1.5 million shares, or almost 3% of shares outstanding as of August 2025. Even with these significant uses of cash in the quarter, our balance sheet remains very strong. We ended the third quarter with cash and cash equivalents of $375 million and no debt. The average daily balance on funds held for clients was approximately $2.5 billion in 2025, up 9% over the prior-year period. Now let me turn to guidance for 2025. Based on our strong year-to-date results, we are well-positioned to meet our full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance ranges. We continue to expect total revenue to be between $2.045 billion and $2.055 billion, up 9% year-over-year at the midpoint of the range.
Within revenues, we expect organic full-year recurring and other revenue to be up 10% year-over-year, and interest on funds held for clients to be down 10% year-over-year to $113 million, assuming one additional rate cut later this year. Our full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance range is $872 million to $882 million, representing year-over-year adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 160 basis points to near-record levels at approximately 43% at the midpoint of the range. Other forward-looking items include full-year GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates of 27% and 26%, respectively, and stock compensation of approximately 7% of revenues.
We delivered strong results in the third quarter and reinvested our capital into data centers while at the same time returning significant cash to shareholders through buybacks and dividends. 2025 has been a strong year, and we are well-positioned for a robust 2026 and beyond.
